summary: Reproduced EXIF Orientation being ignored by the CPU byte loader and direct-PIL loader, and confirmed that both GPU JPEG routes would return an untransformed tensor. Rotated JPEGs now use Pillow's canonical EXIF transpose while orientation 1 or absent retains the existing GPU fast paths.

tests.what_was_measured: Before: Orientation=6 decoded as (24, 16) instead of (16, 24), pixels differed from ImageOps.exif_transpose, direct PIL retained raw dimensions, and both mocked GPU decoders were called. After: CPU and direct-PIL outputs were pixel-identical with (16, 24), and both GPU decoders were bypassed. Raw logs: reports/j-fa74d1441e28/raw/before_reproduction.txt and after_reproduction.txt.
17 tests passed, including parity with Pillow for EXIF orientations 1-8, direct PIL dimensions, invalid/no-orientation boundaries, and routing for standard and fancy GPU JPEG decoders.
No whitespace errors in the proposed patch.
All applicable repository hooks passed, including AST validation, isort, ruff lint/format, codespell, and CI registry validation.
The prepared interpreter does not include the ruff module; no lint result was claimed.

gpu_execution_evidence: The assigned device was visible as AMD Instinct MI350X with ROCm 7.2, but sglang.srt.utils.common.is_cuda() returned false. The affected GPU JPEG branches are NVIDIA-only and were therefore tested through deterministic routing mocks, not executed on gfx950. See reports/j-fa74d1441e28/raw/gpu_environment.txt.
remaining_limitations: No NVIDIA GPU was assigned, so actual torchvision nvJPEG and nvImageCodec decode execution was not validated. No model/server run was performed because the defect and correction are confined to deterministic image ingestion and require neither weights nor serving. Malformed EXIF behavior is fail-open to the unrotated image by design.
